## Design

### 2026-11-01: 1 Nov: Components & Schematic

**1h**

1 Nov: Components & Schematic

For this project, I decided to create a small gaming console similar to the Switch to play the only dinosaur game. I plan to add more games later, but for now this will do.

Designing the Schematic:
The Switch 2 has 2 sides, each with an analog stick and 4 buttons. I think that 8 buttons and 2 sticks are a bit overkill for any game that will ever grace this device, so i will do one side; I don't know, but i think it's now much more similar to arcade game controllers. This is my current vision

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/0c405013238f9f8246391701fce337b217d638293760f268c8ca52413c7987b9.png)

For the MCU, I will again use the ESP-32S-30 pin, which I already used in previous projects due to its availability in the local market. I may also create another smaller version using the ESP-32-C3, but not now ig.

I will also add a vibrating disk motor, because why not. It is funny that the joystick module is much less expensive on Amazon than the stick alone. This is the module I chose (HALJIA PS2 Game Joystick Axis Sensor Module).

After connecting the components to the corresponding pins, here is the final schematic

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/b8d345e5c16c99286533de3d47b8941b00021c15805ed9d749e0bdcc297a7050.png)
Oops, looks like I forgot to add the joystick module, so I added it real quick and added its correct footprint, and here is the final schematic.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/e694abcfbf0f44f410ff7c6f0eac5b08f62c2643ffd2a8fcf8673fb33f4719c0.png)

### 2026-11-02: Nov 2: PCB

**4h**

Nov 2: PCB

I made some changes to the motor circuit. I will swap the N-channel MOSFET, which requires 1 voltage of at least 5v to work properly. I didn't know this since i copied the circuit from a YouTube tutorial that used Arduino instead of ESP-32. I watched another tutorial that fully explains the circuit and how to set it up. This tutorial uses a transistor instead of the MOSFET,

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mgwWh6gVGCo

I couldn't find the transistor used in the tutorial, but I ended up using the 2N2222 Transistor, which has a max current of 600 milli amp. This makes it more than capable of handling the motor

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/133ef56fd3bfd468931c3b49c0c9a8268b9d3d59023d27bfcdd431b89534622c.png)

I placed all the components and organized them to resemble a console. The joystick module will stick out of the PCB, mainly to save costs since there is no point in making it part of the PCB.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/78add66e67449677f50b838b46a8bc2586aeec2fe42399462ffd6bfc50a8f9a7.png)

The PCB after some routing, This time I want to make the routing as clean as possible.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/74ad57e0445fa66631a976286216cd07b046e940a9981cf479529b7c3dd5b20e.png)

The current configuration looks weird to me. I just had an idea, which is separating the microcontroller from the rest of the parts, but to do this, I will need to create 2 boards and connect them with a bundle of wires.
I added a connector to help with connecting the wires for each part.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/b871899c135558a1d97fd10e94881fc8af4734808cd57d00a95fcd0663167cba.png)

This is the Shcematic after some organization and cleanup.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/0e12dcde6b03c9dc8ea564498b5743a49026ceb2607db7c95b735c409e6b4c71.png)
